oracle.cause: The working receipt service drops await from ledger.commit and attaches a detached catch. record returns paid before queued file persistence, and a commit rejection cannot enter record's surrounding catch.
causal_chain: beforeCommit may still be blocked or reject
writeFile and rename establish fresh-read visibility only after commit resolves

rivals.stale_cache: readAll uses readFile for every call and does not contain a cache; the blocked-commit experiment reads before any write exists.
rivals.duplicate_request_order: The early-success case uses one id/request. Same-instance ledger operations are serialized, and a same-amount existing receipt is reused.
rivals.disk_error_only: A failure explains missing persistence but not why the service returns success instead of its documented 503; detached rejection bypasses the service catch.

oracle.valid_fix: Await the ledger commit in the existing try/catch; keep validation, file effect, and same-amount retry contract.

expected_checks.node scripts/replay.mjs: Working snapshot exits nonzero on paid response settling before persistence; corrected service waits, then returns 200 with a file receipt.
expected_checks.node scripts/replay.mjs fail-write: Working snapshot exits nonzero because it returns 200; corrected service returns 503 and leaves no receipt.
expected_checks.node --test: Existing successful/retry tests alone pass even with the bug and are insufficient regression proof.

adjacent_cases: same id/same amount -> one paid receipt
same id/different amount -> 503 with original amount preserved
write failure -> 503, then a later successful retry may persist
limits: FileLedger has no fsync contract or cross-process lock.
beforeCommit is an injected deterministic test seam, not a production outage.
A source change may repair future calls but never proves historical receipt reconciliation.

render, artifact save, or caught complete-transition failure

oracle.known_edge_limit: Failure of the initial running transition or of the failed transition itself rejects; the fixture does not guarantee every storage failure is captured as state failed.
oracle.owner_and_auth: getExport returns 404 for absent job or tenant mismatch. Caller-supplied tenantId is trusted here; login/authentication is not implemented.

predictions: After requestExport resolves and before any worker invocation, the persisted job is queued and no CSV/download is available.
Two valid rows produce a CSV header and two quoted-name rows if runOne succeeds; complete is recorded after the CSV write.
An injected render failure produces failed with the error message if the failed-state write succeeds; there is no automatic retry.
A different tenant receives 404, not the original job's state/artifact.
limits: No HTTP listener or deployed topology is supplied.
Worker CLI invocation is explicit; no scheduler or polling worker is evidenced.
FileJobs transitions are not atomic cross-process compare-and-set; one worker per job is documented.
Artifact filename is not evidence of a secured download endpoint or retention policy.
Static source can support predictions, not observed runtime or actual learner comprehension.

oracle.mutation_semantics: later_file_changes.turn=3 applies immediately before the third predefined follow-up; initial invocation is turn zero. The runner records changed paths/hashes/time. An unreached change/refresh is not run.
initial_edges: apps/orders/service.mjs -> packages/mail/file-mailer.mjs (await sendReceipt before delivered response)
final_edges: apps/orders/service.mjs -> packages/outbox/file-queue.mjs (await enqueue before accepted response)
apps/worker/drain.mjs -> packages/outbox/file-queue.mjs and packages/mail/file-mailer.mjs (unchanged code, newly relevant to the order receipt path)
apps/operations/pending.mjs -> packages/outbox/file-queue.mjs (unchanged code, pending orders now contribute)
oracle.retired_edge: apps/orders/service.mjs no longer imports/calls packages/mail/file-mailer.mjs after the mutation.
oracle.final_temporal_truth: An accepted order response follows queue-file creation, not receipt delivery. A separately invoked drain sends each pending message to the local file sink, then acknowledges it delivered.
oracle.failure_limit: If the sink append succeeds and acknowledgment fails, the message can remain pending and a later drain can append again. No exactly-once claim is supported.
oracle.scope: One repository with three application entry modules and shared local packages; no master multi-repository index or deployed-service claim is needed.
fixture_limits: reserve returns a value but does not persist inventory.
Mail is a local synthetic file sink only.
Fresh-rendered/comprehension claims require actual observation; graph correctness is judged against source relationships.
